transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Hurricane Isaias is gaining strength in the warm Gulf of Mexico and is forecast to make
landfall as early as tonight on the northern Gulf Coast.
And Pierre's Debbie Elliott reports it's now a powerful Category 3 hurricane packing
120 mile per hour winds.
National Hurricane Center director Michael Brennan says Isaias is on track to hit Northwest
Florida.
This powerful hurricane expected to make landfall this evening into the late night hours and
then move quickly inland across portions of the Florida Panhandle and up into Alabama
as we go through the overnight hours into Saturday.
He says hazards will be a storm surge of 6 to 9 feet, damaging winds and rainfall up
to 15 inches.
Brennan says expect widespread power outages, tornadoes and flash flooding as the storm
moves inland over the southeastern U.S.
Isaias is the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, which has until now been dampened
by a strong El Nino weather pattern.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Crestview, Florida.
The Chicago Bears are paying tribute to an NFL giant affectionately known as Iron Mike
and the coach.
Mike Ditka died this morning at the age of 86.
On the website, the team says Ditka had an immeasurable impact on the Bears organization
over decades as a player, coach and ambassador.
He led the team to a Super Bowl victory after the 1985 season.
Three years later, rather in 1988, he was inducted into the NFL Hall of Fame where he
delivered a brief speech.
In life, many men have talent, but talent in itself is no accomplishment.
Excellence in football and excellence in life is bred when men recognize their opportunities
and then pursue them with a passion.
The team also writes of Ditka's larger-than-life personality being captured in commercials
and TV programs such as Cheers, Saturday Night Live and L.A. Law.
Israel has firmly condemned the decision to award South African human rights pioneer and
judge Navi Pillay the Nobel Peace Prize.
Pillay recently oversaw the UN Commission report that concluded Israel committed genocide
in Gaza.
Here's NPR's Kat Von Stor.
When the UN Commission released its report last year, Pillay said, "It is clear that
there is an intent to destroy the Palestinians in Gaza through acts that meet the criteria
set forth in the Genocide Convention."
She said the responsibility for such actions lies with the highest Israeli authorities.
Israel has strongly rejected those findings.
In reaction to Pillay's award, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Nobel
Committee has "lost its moral compass" while Israel's Foreign Ministry said the committee
was rewarding "the biggest lie of the 21st century."
Pillay has been a judge on several international criminal courts overseeing many issues.
The Nobel Committee's announcement of the prize made no mention of Israel.
Kat Wandsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
It's NPR. In Alaska last night, the state's gubernatorial candidates held a debate.
Alaska Public Media's Eric Stone has a recap.
Three Republicans are facing off against a Democrat in the race to be Alaska's next governor.
Democrat Jonathan Christ Tompkins has a lead over the fractured Republican field.
He's positioning himself as a pragmatic moderate.
We need to be able to work together to find common ground, to bridge where there's disagreement,
and that's what's going to move Alaska forward.
The top polling Republican is business owner Bernadette Wilson.
She said she'd fight efforts to raise taxes on oil companies as Alaska stares down a budget
crunch.
I am up for that battle.
I do not want a governor that's going to concede the fight before they even get started.
Several recent polls showed the Democrat winning as voters sour on President Trump and Alaska's
incumbent Republican governor.
For NPR News, I'm Eric Stone in Anchorage.
Authorities in Russia say they've lifted all public health restrictions following the death
of a 28-year-old lab worker at a plague research institute in Siberia.
NPR's Charles Mains reports from Moscow, the woman's death, raise concerns about a potential
outbreak of plague or some other deadly pathogen.
Ever since the death of a female lab technician in Russia's Irkutsk region last week, Russian
health authorities have insisted she succumbed to an unknown form of pneumonia rather than
the plague.
Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobsov, all but declared that version final, Kobsov said the deceased
lab technician had been vaccinated and was immune to the deadly pathogen she worked with.
He also said thousands of tests found no evidence of infection among other lab workers and that
life in Irkutsk would be going back to normal.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
U.S. stocks trading higher with the Dow now up more than 400 points.
This is NPR News.
